subject: Switchability & priced ramp — term scenarios for Velocity Labs
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@velocitylabs.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@velocitylabs.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — pricing flexibility + migration credits

Connor —

Thanks for the proposal you shared earlier. We're evaluating a path off our incumbent (SkyForge) and want to understand how Redwood would structure a ramped pricing deal if we commit to a 12–18 month transition. A few specific asks from procurement and engineering: 

- Can you show a staged price ladder (consumption tiers) with a short-term introductory rate for months 1–3?
- Are there migration credits or implementation allowances tied to usage milestones?
- What packaging options exist for mixed seat + consumption customers (we run a mix of API traffic and a small fleet of dedicated inference jobs)?

Procurement is also asking if Redwood can align net economics with SkyForge's most recent term sheet — specifically a blended effective price around $0.006/token for month 4–12 if we achieve the target throughput. If you can match or come close, we can accelerate sign-off.

Can we set a 30-minute sync tomorrow? I can share the SkyForge term extract if it helps.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
VP of Platform & Procurement
Velocity Labs

Attachment: vendor-comparison-extract.txt (plain text excerpt of SkyForge pricing)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elena@velocitylabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — pricing flexibility + migration credits

Elena — thanks, and appreciate the clarity. I got the SkyForge extract and reviewed it with Karthik (pricing workstream). Quick take below and a proposed next step.

Short answers up front: we can put together a staged/ramped price ladder and a migration allowance that ties to runbook milestones and verified traffic handover. We don't usually advertise a public $/token anchor that low without commitment, but we can design a blended structure that meets your target economics over the contract term with the right throughput and onboarding credits.

Concretely I will:
- Attach a concise commercial proposal with two lanes: (A) 12-month staged consumption with onboarding credits; (B) 18-month blended commitment with higher credits and a two-month introductory introductory rate.
- Include an explicit seat+consumption packaging example (how calls are metered, seat entitlements, and a sample invoice glidepath).
- Flag a technical compatibility credit we call the "runtime handover" allowance — it offsets extra ops cost during the first 6 weeks of cutover.

Propose a 30-minute call 10/29 at 10am PT to walk the tradeoffs. If procurement wants legal redlines in parallel, we can accept a short redline window (we'll review DocuSign + redlines).

I'll attach the proposal (PDF) and a short spreadsheet that maps line items to the SkyForge comparators so you can present that to your CFO.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-proposal-velocity-20261028.pdf; velocity-term-questions.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-28T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — pricing mechanics and counter scenarios

Connor — looping through our preferred counter constructs so we present clean options on the call. Notes for the proposal: 

1) Staged consumption ladder (Option A) — low intro for first 60 days ($0.0045/token capped at X tokens), step to $0.007/token for months 3–6, then to $0.006 on blended basis for remainder if velocity thresholds met. Provide a usage corridor and an overage collar so Velocity's CFO can model worst-case.

2) Blended commitment (Option B) — 18-month commitment with monthly true-up. We bake in onboarding credits upfront (equal to ~3–5% of committed spend) plus a separate runtime handover credit (one-time). This gets closer to the $0.006 blended target without needing an aggressive month-1 intro.

3) Seat + Consumption packaging — define a per-seat monthly fee for developer/engineer access (entitlement to dedicated concurrency) and a consumption pool with prioritized routing. For simplicity show a sample: 10 seats + 250M tokens/month pool.

4) Migration credit mechanics — credits issued as invoice offsets on milestone acceptance (pilot completion, routing cutover, first 30 days post-cutover). Keep credit pay-out tied to verifiable metrics to avoid open-ended credits.

5) Concessions we can make: limited-term price match to SkyForge for months 4–12 if Velocity provides a committed minimum throughput and a clear rollback clause. We should avoid open-ended equivalence beyond 12 months.

I'll be on the call 10/29 to run the commercial scenarios and answer any runtime-fit questions.

Karthik
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

Connor / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turn. Procurement reviewed the attachment and likes Option B (18-month blended commitment) as it reduces budget volatility. A few follow-ups before our internal decision: 

- Can Redwood commit to the migration credit flow described (invoice offsets at pilot completion and 30-day post-cutover)? Procurement needs the mechanism documented.
- Will you provide a one-page summary that directly maps Redwood line items to the SkyForge terms (I can give you the exact SkyForge clause IDs if useful)?
- Legal wants to see a draft term sheet that includes a rollback clause and a defined SLA credit for sustained latency > 300ms for inference endpoints (we flagged that with infra).

If you can provide the draft term sheet + the one-page comparators by EOD Monday, we will review and aim for a formal procurement meeting the following week.

We are willing to commit to the throughput thresholds required for the blended $0.006 effective rate if the migration credits and rollback protections are in place. Also copying SkyForge's sales contact — they have asked to be kept in the loop during any formal negotiation.

Regards,
Elena Morales
VP of Platform & Procurement, Velocity Labs
